name: context-menu
purpose: A Menu (WAI-ARIA APG Menu, same engine as Menu: submenus, checkbox and radio items, typeahead, overlay stack) opened on the contextmenu event at the pointer position, or from the keyboard with Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key at the focused element inside the target. The native browser menu stays reachable with Shift+right-click (nativeModifier 'shift') or while disabled. The popup is a Menu popup and needs @absoluteui/components/menu/style.css as well.
whenToUse: Shortcuts to commands for an object under the pointer (rows, files, canvas objects) that are also available elsewhere in the UI.
Per-row commands in a list or table, using the origin in the select detail to find the row.
whenNotToUse: As the only way to reach an action: context menus are hard to discover and unavailable on many touch devices; always provide a visible control (for example a Menu button) too.
Replacing the browser menu on text content where users expect copy, paste, spell check, or 'open link in new tab'.
Choosing a form value: use Select, Combobox, or Radio Group.
Rich interactive content: use Popover or Dialog.
states: open at an element (keyboard or open() without a point)
responsive: Popup width at least 12rem (Menu maximum min(22rem, 100vw - 1rem)); height capped by popover-max-height and the available viewport space, then scrolls. The positioning engine flips and shifts every level to stay in the viewport; the pointer anchor follows the target when the page scrolls.
rtl: direction 'rtl' (option or global direction) aligns the popup with bottom-start mirrored, opens submenus to the left, swaps ArrowLeft/ArrowRight for submenus, and mirrors the submenu chevron via [data-direction='rtl']. An inherited dir=rtl alone does not switch it.
theme: Uses the Menu styles and tokens; the context-menu stylesheet only adds a minimum inline size and uses no tokens.
security: Labels, descriptions, shortcuts, and group labels are rendered with textContent; never parsed as HTML. Styles only through compiled CSS and the CSSOM. CSP-safe.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Checkbox and radio state lives in memory and is reset by update({ items }).

performance.testedScale: 200 items in one level; three nested levels; one context menu per target.

limitations: The target gets no ARIA attributes: nothing announces that a context menu exists. Add a visible or described hint (for example aria-describedby text such as 'Press Shift+F10 for actions') and provide every action elsewhere.

nativeModifier applies to pointer right-clicks only: inside an enabled target Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key always open the component menu, so the native menu is not reachable from the keyboard there.
One item list per instance; vary items per origin with update({ items }) from a capture-phase contextmenu listener on the target.
The pointer anchor is fixed relative to the target's box; when the target itself is a scroll container, scrolling its content does not move the menu.
Keyboard-generated contextmenu events are recognized heuristically (button other than 2 at client point 0,0); browsers that report other coordinates open at that point instead of the focused element.
Popups are appended to the target's enclosing <dialog> or to <body> at construction; moving the target into or out of a dialog afterwards needs destroy() and create().
unsupported: Touch long-press opening (only the browser's contextmenu event, which some touch browsers fire on long press).
Rendering HTML or custom nodes inside items.
Link items (href); handle navigation in the aui-select listener.
Context menus on nested targets: the event bubbles to the outer target, which opens its own menu too (the outer menu ends up open) unless a listener on the inner target stops propagation.
antiPatterns: Actions that exist only in a context menu.
Suppressing the native menu on large text areas or whole pages.
Deeply nested submenus (more than two levels).

adapters.angular: @absoluteui/angular/context-menu: AuiContextMenu directive on the target ([auiContextMenu]="items", contextMenuLabel, contextMenuDisabled); outputs auiSelect, auiOpen, auiClose.
